materialized_by: Claude Opus 5.5, under HPO-ODS-01, as the authorized primary development executor. Not an owner, not a certifier.
WHY: The recertification of 979b1440 failed OEP-1: the route-B plaintext reached PostgreSQL and was measured in logs through the CONTEXT line of the nested EXECUTE, while a closed list of logging settings said PASS. The owner removed the plaintext from the server boundary; this amendment carries that into the channel, rebuilds OEP-1 around PLAINTEXT_PASSWORD_SERVER_EXPOSURE = IMPOSSIBLE_BY_CONSTRUCTION, binds the session, and re-pins the channel.

PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.route_b: db/custody/mint-route-b-contract.ts ROUTE_B_STATEMENTS: SET_VERIFIER binds the client-derived verifier; the DO block refuses (D1_VERIFIER_REQUIRED) any value not in SCRAM-SHA-256 format before the ALTER ROLE; RB-DELTA-4.
PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.derivation: db/custody/scram-verifier.ts semantics (RFC 5802/7677, PostgreSQL format SCRAM-SHA-256$<iter>:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>), reproduced byte-exactly against the RFC 7677 exchange; the mint tool derives it inline.
PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.entropy: Governed, not chosen: capability SECRET_GENERATION_CONTRACT.generation_requirements.entropy ('At least 32 bytes from a cryptographically secure random source'); base64url, on which SASLprep is the identity.
PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.iterations_and_salt: PostgreSQL defaults (4096 iterations, 16-byte CSPRNG salt): what the server itself would use.
PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.plaintext_path: The plaintext exists only in the mint tool: it derives the verifier and, after the database act, goes to the N30 depositor stdin (OT-15). It is never in statement text, bind values, startup parameters, server-side variables or functions.
PASSWORD_TRANSPORT.verifier_is_not_directly_usable: Authentication needs ClientKey-derived proof; the verifier holds StoredKey = H(ClientKey). Stated limits: StoredKey plus a CAPTURED exchange yields ClientKey; ServerKey lets its holder impersonate the server. Measured: the verifier used as a password fails (disposable proof).

OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.central_invariant: PLAINTEXT_PASSWORD_SERVER_EXPOSURE = IMPOSSIBLE_BY_CONSTRUCTION. OEP-1 no longer asks a server whether it would log the plaintext: the plaintext never reaches it. The probe proves the SESSION the mint will use.

what_the_probe_proves.TARGET_SESSION_BOUND: current_user = session_user = the operator principal; current_database() = the route-B database; server_version_num >= 100000 (SCRAM verifiers accepted) — observed inside the session on the N04 host and route-B port the tool bound.
what_the_probe_proves.STARTUP_PARAMETERS_CLOSED: the settings whose source is 'client' are EXACTLY the measured postgres.js 3.4.9 set (application_name=postgres.js, client_encoding=UTF8): no startup GUC rode in.
what_the_probe_proves.PROBE_MINT_CONFIGURATION_COHERENT: host, port, database, principal, driver digest and startup set of the probe session = those the mint session will use (session fingerprint).

OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.what_it_no_longer_infers: Whether any logging setting, extension, hook or lock wait would record the PLAINTEXT. That class is open (the recertification's finding) and is closed by construction instead.
OEP1_PROBE_CONTRACT.derived_material_exposure: Informational classification of whether the VERIFIER could be logged (POSSIBLE / NOT_INDICATED / UNKNOWN; never 'absent'). It gates nothing about the plaintext and is never merged with PLAINTEXT_NOT_PRESENT.

statements.DERIVED_MATERIAL_SETTINGS: SELECT name, setting, source FROM pg_catalog.pg_settings WHERE name = ANY($1::text[]) ORDER BY name

TLS_TRUST_BOUNDARY.status: OPEN_OWNER_BOUNDARY — not decided here, not weakened here
TLS_TRUST_BOUNDARY.measured: Both tools connect with ssl: 'require', which in postgres.js 3.4.9 means rejectUnauthorized = false: the session is encrypted but the server is not authenticated. postgres.js 3.4.9 implements no SCRAM channel binding (no -PLUS mechanism).
TLS_TRUST_BOUNDARY.consequence: A man-in-the-middle holding a certificate could relay the operator's SCRAM exchange and act inside the privileged session (for instance install a verifier of its own choosing). The plaintext fix does NOT depend on TLS (the plaintext is never sent) and is not weakened by this.
TLS_TRUST_BOUNDARY.why_not_implemented: Verifying the server needs a root of trust (which CA, pinned how). No D-1 authority governs it; the repository's operator runner (db/hosted/operator-runner.ts) requires verify-full with an operator-supplied PGSSLROOTCERT but fixes no CA identity. Choosing one is a trust-policy decision reserved to the owner.
